card.band: 8 h. About 25 warning kinds, each an independent lever with a different subtle rule set. A frontier agent covers the common ones and misses the semantic ones (format-string, table-operations, unreachable code). A weaker model implements a few.

card.grading: The repo's Linter.test.cpp cases (adapted) plus a few thousand hidden Luau snippets with expected warning code, line and message text, generated by running the upstream linter. The base fails every case. Credit is per lint rule bucket.
card.task: /app ships a history-less snapshot at the base, with Analysis/src/Linter.cpp reduced to a stub that reports no warnings. The agent rebuilds the lint passes (unknown/deprecated globals, unused locals/imports, shadowing, misleading and/or, comparison mistakes, format-string checks, deprecated API, table literal duplicates, integer parsing, etc.) using the public Luau::lint API and warning codes.

spike.notes: The build at tag 0.743 took 13 min with 3 jobs. The Linter suite (105 cases, 468 assertions) passed 3 of 3 runs with byte-identical output. Linter.cpp is 3667 lines and there are 29 warning codes. The 60 snippets produced byte-identical luau-analyze output over two runs, and 15 or more lint kinds fired. The luau-analyze output includes TypeError lines, so type-inference-dependent output must be filtered or excluded from the hidden set. I did not run the full 5.5k-case unit suite three times. start_scores_zero is false only because of the 26 negative cases; every positive-warning case fails on the stub. offline_ok is by inference, not a measured offline run, because the build needs only a local CMake build with no downloads.

spike_plan.kill_if: Build fails or is nondeterministic, or lint output varies between runs (K4), or the rules cannot be isolated per code.
spike_plan.pass_if: Build finishes offline in under 60 min, suite is deterministic over 3 runs, stubbed base fails all Linter cases, and lint output is byte-identical across repeated runs on 50 snippets.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone luau-lang/luau at tag 0.743 (no history beyond the tag).
Build Luau.UnitTest and the CLI with CMake Release on 8 cores; record wall time (smoke probe did not run, so this is the first build check).
Run ./build/Luau.UnitTest --reporters=console --no-colors and confirm the Linter test cases pass and are deterministic across 3 runs.
Stub Linter.cpp to report nothing and confirm Linter.test.cpp cases fail (base must fail every case).
Write 50 random snippets covering 10 rules (e.g. unknown global, format string, table duplicate); run the CLI lint on each twice and diff output for determinism.
Check that the pinned message text and line numbers are stable between runs; note any rule whose output depends on type inference state.

v1.summary: The seed is real and sealable: Luau 0.743 is MIT, Linter.cpp (3,667 lines) and the test file are present at the tag, and the grading surface is thousands of snippets with an executable oracle. Passing requires conditions: pin the exact message strings in the spec, since a different valid implementation would otherwise fail on text, and size the tier to 20 h because a strong agent needs about 11 h for the full scope (the 8 h tier makes a 0.9-of-reference pass unlikely).

v2.note: Strongest card. Confirmed: tag 0.743, a 3.7k-line Linter.cpp (about 3.0k code lines), a 2.8k-line Linter.test.cpp, MIT licence and a public lint-code reference page. The upstream linter is an executable oracle for unlimited hidden snippets, and per-rule buckets give natural partial credit. Visible tests pin the message text, so the grading is fair. Check that the rules depending on type information stay deterministic, and keep the Luau CLI out of the image. With an 11 h frontier estimate, an 8-20 h tier fits; the spike should settle which.
